Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement here at Nebula has asked me to move this forward quickly. We need a binding reserved-capacity commitment for Q1–Q3 2027 to support our pilot rollout. Key asks from legal/procurement: a clear workback schedule for provisioning, and an explicit price-floor clause (we need assurance that unit pricing will not exceed agreed floor + a defined indexation mechanism).

High-level numbers: starting 250 GPU-hours/day (mixed A100-like / 80% batch, 20% low-latency), scaling to 800 GPU-hours/day by month 3. We expect monthly ramp milestones.

Can you provide: 1) a provisioning workback with dates and handoffs, 2) the price-floor language/thresholds you can commit to, and 3) the internal approval path (who signs off on discounts / price protections)? Procurement will need this for our SOW and to confirm with our CFO.

If helpful, procurement is available for a quick call this Thursday 10/22 at 11am PT.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
Nebula Health

3) Lauren: prepare suggested contract language for a price-floor + indexation mechanism we can propose to Nebula legal.

Karthik — quick read and preliminary numbers. I ran a sensitivity run and attached the raw model (pricing-impact-model.csv). Summary:
- Baseline (no floor, list price): blended unit cost estimate $0.72/token-equivalent-hour.
- Hard price floor set at 15% below list increases Redwood's exposure if GPU spot costs spike; worst-case P&L impact over 12 months (assuming a 40% GPU-cost surge) is ~ $620k gross.
- Discount authority: Sales org can approve up to a 12% blended discount off list without Sr. Finance approval. Any effective floor that implies >12% average discount versus list requires VP/Finance sign-off. For a permanent floor + indexation, VP approval recommended.

Recommended approach to get momentum without exec delay:
1) Offer a tiered floor: months 1–3 floor at 12% off list (internal approval), months 4–12 evaluate with a 12–18% collar contingent on GPU-cost index triggers and a 30-day notice clause for adjustments.
2) Require Nebula to commit to a minimum monthly utilization (we used 70% of tranche capacity in the model) to mitigate tail risk.

If Sales wants a cleaner approval path for the customer PO, I can route a VP approval memo. Need a final signed term sheet and expected monthly spend to size the memo.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Finance — Redwood Inference

Karthik / Marissa — thank you both, that helps clarify. Procurement is comfortable with a tiered floor as long as the term sheet clearly shows the ramp tranches and minimum monthly utilization. We are agreeable to the proposed months 1–3 12% floor (internal approval) with a conditional months 4–12 collar up to 18% pending the index trigger language. We will also include a PO with minimum monthly spend tied to the tranche schedule.

Please include the DocuSign link in your next email. If you can get VP memo routed by EOD Monday, that will speed internal approvals on our side.
